newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - AUSTRALIAN GENERAL NEWS - MARCH 6.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - AUSTRALIAN GENERAL NEWS - MARCH 6.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Despite the release of figures from the Australian Bureau of Statistics that indicate sluggish growth in the economy for the December quarter, the Federal Government is sticking to its ambitious prediction of 3.5 per cent economic growth in 1996-97. The ABS figures showed the economy grew by 0.5 per cent in the quarter after seasonal adjustment. Page 1.

The introduction of the Federal Government's Workplace Relations Act has placed unions in a difficult situation in spreading federal award regulation to new employers. The Australian Industrial Relations Commission has already heard several cases involving legal doubts about the status of the so-called 'roping-in' awards, which is the traditional method used by unions to extend award coverage. Page 2.

The scene has been set for a fiery Premiers Conference this month: Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett has called on the Federal Government to put its house in order, and accused it of failing to govern; while other State premiers have stepped up the pressure against further Federal Budget cuts. Page 5.

A major study by Access Economics for Tourism Council Australia, the Tourism Task Force and the Property Council of Australia has been used in the pre-Budget submission that calls on the Federal Government not to make funding cuts to the Australian Tourism Commission. The report underlines the critical role of the ATC. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Federal Government has called on one of Australia's most experienced former bureaucrats Ken Baxter to help devise a system to check on politicians and their perks. The proposed new system, expected to be installed by May, follows mounting evidence that the existing system is unable to minimise rorts. Page 1.

David Helfgott, the subject of Australian film Shine, which has been nominated for seven Oscars, opened his North American tour in typical style last night: the critics were unhappy, the audience at the Boston Symphony Hall was ecstatic, and Helfgott, who suffers from a mental illness, had a ball. Page 1.

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello said yesterday low inflation and moderate growth would be the basis for a speed-up in the pace of economic activity during this year. Despite new figures showing the economy had expanded just 0.5 per cent in the December uarter, Costello stuck to his target of 3.75 per cent growth by June. Page 1.

Cairns schoolboy Tjandamurra O'Shane's mother, Jenni Patterson, said last night the death penalty would be too good for Paul Wade Streeton, who was found guilty yesterday of attempting to kill O'Shane. Streeton faces a maximum of life imprisonment for the attempted killing. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The New South Wales Police Royal Commission heard yesterday children at State public schools could still be at risk because the Department of School Education has not monitored teachers reprimanded for sexual misconduct. The Commission heard that all of the 106 teachers were still working in the State's public schools. Page 1.

Federal Science Minister Peter McGauran told Parliament yesterday the Federal Government endorsed a plan to use Australia's Synroc for treating the high-level spent rods at Lucas Heights, and also said developing a reprocessing plant was one option being considered by Cabinet in reaction to the storage problems being faced at the research reactor in Sydney's south. Page 1.

In a blow to the union movement, the Federal Government will allow its own departments and agencies to negotiate non-union individual work contracts with employees, and will also end the automatic deduction of membership dues for the bulk of its own 130,00 workers. Page1.

New South Wales Police Minister Paul Whelan yesterday said the "gross incompetence" of police may have allowed some of the 29 victims of a suspected serial rapist to suffer their fate. Whelan has called for the sacking of officers involved in the investiation who lost critical evidence including semen samples, a balaclava used by the rapist, and a torch. Page 1.
THE AGE

At a meeting in Canberra last night, Federal Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith told the ACTU and other union representatives that the Federal Government's 130,000 public servants must shift on to individual or agency-based contracts as part of an overhaul of the national bureaucracy. Page A1.

Primary Industries Minister John Anderson yesterday confirmed that three consignments of Australian processed meat and milk products were being held by South Korean authorities because of fears resulting from Victoria's anthrax outbreak. Anderson said other Asian countries, including Thailand, held similar fears, yet had been reassured the outbreak was under control. Page A1.

A report tabled in Parliament yesterday by the National Audit Office into the Army Presence in the North Program has found the transfer of forces to Australia's future battleground, has been badly affected by the discovery that tanks cannot shoot straight in the hot climate, soldiers risk heat exhaustion and costs have been blown out. Page A1.

Martin Brundle was back at turn three at Albert Park yesterday, still amazed at his escape on that same turn in the Melbourne Grand Prix last year in which his car cartwheeled through the corner at 200 kilometres an hour. This year Brundle will be facing the track from the TV commentary box. Page A1.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
